issues.description: The abstract method messageOnFeed() has conflicting return types across artifacts. The problem statement UML and exercise description specify Animal.messageOnFeed(): String (see problem_statement.md UML). In the solution, Animal.java declares public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java:18) and a new helper class FeedResponse is introduced (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/FeedResponse.java). Some concrete implementations (Seal, Pig) return FeedResponse, but Goat.java incorrectly overrides messageOnFeed() with a String return type (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java:10), which causes a compile-time signature mismatch. The Farm implementation calls System.out.println(a.messageOnFeed()) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java:27-31), which masks the mismatch at runtime due to FeedResponse.toString(), but the differing method signatures (String vs FeedResponse) are a structural contradiction that will confuse students and may cause compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the messageOnFeed() signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix to match the problem statement: change Animal.messageOnFeed() in the solution to return String (e.g. public abstract String messageOnFeed();) and update all concrete classes (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return the specified String messages ("Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"). Remove the FeedResponse class (or stop using it as the method return type). Update Farm and any callers to treat messageOnFeed() as returning String. Alternatively, if FeedResponse is intentionally required as part of an extended design, update the problem statement and UML to document FeedResponse as the return type and ensure all concrete classes override messageOnFeed() with FeedResponse (and update template/tests accordingly).
